Alex K: ran a profiling sweep on the MoE routing stack this morning, found weird spikes during token dispatch + KV cache refill
Maria T: can you paste the trace?
Alex K: short dump below, 3-GPU tensor+pipeline setup, 8 experts, batch=64, seq=128
Alex K: ```
# run: ./tools/profile --model=model_v7 --gpus=3 --mp=1 --pp=3 --moe-experts=8 --batch=64 --seq=128 --profiler=nvtx
Time breakdown (p50/p95/p99): compute 12/45/78 ms, all-reduce 3/12/30 ms, all-to-all 6/40/85 ms, KV cache refill 0.5/8/22 ms
nvprof flags: All-to-all shows heavy tails on some ranks (rank1 rank2) during routing windows
```
Chloe R: ouch, all-to-all p99 85ms is rough. does this line up with the new kernel selection changes from last deploy?
Alex K: that's my suspicion — we changed the attention kernel selection heuristics in 176k deploy to favor the fused matmul kernel for short seqs, might have increased memory pressure on expert queues + gated dispatch timings
Paul S: I also saw KV cache GC kicking around the same timestamps in our logs. Could be memory reclamation stalls overlapping comm.
Alex K: attached flamegraph snapshot (trimmed): major pause at router_enqueue -> all_to_all -> recv_wait -> kv_cache_load
Maria T: are the stalls correlated with skewed token distributions? i.e., some experts getting 10x more tokens?
Alex K: yes — skew in top-2 experts is ~8x on this workload. when skew >4x the all-to-all tail balloons.
Maria T: that suggests we need better routing smoothing or backpressure in the routing layer. options: padding redistribution, softmax temperature tuning, dynamic expert dropping, or client-side shard-aware batching.
Paul S: Also can we overlap KV cache loads with comm? right now cache loads happen after we finish splitting tensors for all-to-all. If we prefetch likely-hit keys while comm is in flight we could hide some latency.
Alex K: good point. current code path: gather_kv -> split_for_a2a -> all_to_all (comm) -> apply_expert -> gather_results -> kv_writeback. We could reorder: split_for_a2a -> kick off all_to_all (async) -> prefetch_kv_for_local_experts -> wait_all_to_all -> execute_experts.
Chloe R: Do we have async a2a primitives that let us overlap? NCCL IAllToAll is not universal on our infra. We could emulate with Isend/Irecv but fragility...
Paul S: NCCL 2.12+ has IAllToAll, but need to ensure CUDA streams and comm streams are independent. ops-bot: note: dedicated comm streams are enabled on dedicated clusters only (ops-bot).
ops-bot: dedicated comm streams are enabled in prod-dedicated-1, prod-dedicated-2.
Alex K: I prototyped a change to kick off all-to-all on a separate comm stream and spawn prefetch tasks on compute stream. baseline locally shows ~20% p95 reduction, p99 improves ~35% on synthetic skew 6x.
Alex K: diff snippet: ```cpp
// pseudo
commStream.enqueue(all_to_all_async(send_buf, recv_buf));
computeStream.enqueue(prefetch_kv_for_local_experts());
commStream.synchronize();
computeStream.enqueue(execute_experts());
```
Maria T: that looks promising. any regressions from kernel selection? Alex K: small: fused matmul kernel increased peak memory by ~200MB on 16GB cards, which increased paging/GC frequency on heavily loaded ranks — leads to jitter that amplifies a2a tail.
Chloe R: so two levers: revert/limit fused kernel for MoE configs OR adjust kernel selector to include a memory headroom estimate and avoid the fused kernel when headroom < X.
Paul S: we should also add a router-side adaptive batching heuristic: when one expert gets overloaded, temporarily widen batch splits to spread tokens across more experts (soft balancing) and mark such tokens with lower priority so they get processed in the next micro-batch.
Maria T: can we detect skew cheaply? maybe maintain an exponential moving avg of tokens/expert over 1k steps and trigger when top-1 / median > 3x
Alex K: implemented a lightweight counter in the router, cheap atomic increments, ema on GPU side. detection is sub-ms.
Alex K: quick test plan:
1) run 24h perf job on prod-dedicated-1 with comm stream overlap enabled + kernel-selector headroom change
2) enable router skew detector + soft-balancing fallback
3) capture nvtx and flamegraphs for flagged windows, push results to perf dashboard
Maria T: add canary traffic first, maybe 5% of qps on dedicated cluster. also add automatic fallback to previous deploy if p99 latency regresses >10%.
Chloe R: what about KV cache behavior? do we need to change TTLs or batching of cache writes?
Paul S: correlated pattern: cache refill bursts when a new prefix appears; batching cache writes (delay 2-5ms) reduces write contention but increases memory dwell time. tradeoff depends on latency SLO.
Alex K: for these workloads a 3ms write coalesce reduced KV write IO by 40% with <1% increase in token latency p50. good trade.
Alex K: created a PR with the async a2a prototype + prefetch + kernel-selector tweak and a router detector flag. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3421
Maria T: perf-ci-bot: can you run the nightly perf suite + MoE skewed workload on that PR?
perf-ci-bot: Starting perf run for PR#3421 on prod-dedicated-1 (moe-skewed suite). ETA ~35m. Will post summary on completion. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Paul S: ok let's coordinate rollout: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with ops watch. Chloe can you own kernel-selector change? Maria you own router heuristic. Alex will own async a2a + prefetch. I'll own canary orchestration + metrics.
Chloe R: yes, I'll add a safety flag to disable fused kernel for moegroup if headroom < 500MB
